requirements.requirement: A persistent host firewall is enabled on node1.
requirements.summary: UFW was enabled with an active policy, node1 was rebooted with an acknowledged request and changed boot ID, and UFW plus its complete ruleset remained enabled and active afterward.

requirements.requirement: SSH is allowed to node1 from any IPv4 or IPv6 address.
requirements.summary: The final post-reboot policy contains Anywhere allow rules for TCP/22 for both IPv4 and IPv6. An SSH-port connection from node2 succeeded, and the final lifecycle snapshot shows node1 listening on port 22 on all IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 on node1 is allowed from node2 only.
requirements.summary: The ordered policy allows 10.100.18.11 (node2) before the catch-all rejection. With a confirmed listener running, node2 connected successfully after node1 reboot, and the final rule counter recorded accepted node2 traffic.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 on node1 is rejected from node3 and all other sources.
requirements.summary: Post-reboot testing with a confirmed listener showed node3 receiving an immediate refusal. Final IPv4 and IPv6 catch-all rejection rules were present, and the IPv4 rejection counter recorded matching traffic.

overall_summary: All material firewall outcomes are satisfied. The final, reboot-persistent policy allows SSH globally, permits TCP/9000 from node2, and rejects TCP/9000 from node3 and other IPv4/IPv6 sources. Direct post-reboot connection tests and live counters corroborate the policy. Restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities, and recovered system/network states were captured for all three nodes, with fixed lifecycle boot identities agreeing with the executor observations.
limitations: The provider-wide restart evidence for node1 lacks an unambiguously healthy generic pre-restart state: UFW was active, but ssh.service and ssh.socket were observed failed immediately before the reboot because the connection probes triggered socket activation on a host lacking SSH host keys. Post-restart system state, SSH listeners, UFW state, and lifecycle observations were healthy.

Only node2 and node3 were used as live source hosts. Rejection of every other possible source is established by the directly observed catch-all IPv4 and IPv6 rules rather than exhaustive connection tests from all addresses.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The UFW changes directly implement the task; temporary HTTP listeners were bounded evidence fixtures and were removed; and all three reboots were required by the provider-wide restart protocol. The SSH probes temporarily exposed a pre-existing absence of SSH host keys and left ssh.service/socket failed, but those probes had a clear verification purpose and the subsequent reboot restored port 22 with no failed services. Final snapshots show no test listener or abandoned test files, no failed units, and healthy package state.
